claims.text: The eutectic high-entropy alloy has a multi-phase microstructure with well-defined phase boundaries.
The alloy initially has an intact protective oxide layer.
Mechanical wear repeatedly removes or disrupts the protective oxide layer at elevated temperature.
Oxide removal exposes heterogeneous and reactive phases, grain boundaries, and phase interfaces.
The exposed phase boundaries and interfaces facilitate micro-galvanic interactions.
Micro-galvanic effects promote localized corrosion on the newly exposed surfaces.
Localized corrosion weakens the material and makes it more susceptible to subsequent wear.
The reciprocal interaction between oxide removal, corrosion, and further wear establishes a synergistic degradation feedback loop.
Under simultaneous wear and corrosion, total mass loss will significantly exceed the sum of wear-only and corrosion-only losses.
The wear rate under simultaneous exposure will exceed the wear rate in the matched wear-only baseline.
The corrosion rate under simultaneous exposure will exceed the corrosion rate in the matched corrosion-only baseline.
The proposed synergistic mechanism is expected when the protective oxide is non-self-healing.
A pronounced multi-phase microstructure is a boundary condition for the proposed synergistic mechanism.
Rapid oxide regeneration would reduce the accelerated coupled degradation.
Minimal contrast between phases would reduce the accelerated coupled degradation.

contradictions.description: The design says all groups are tested under matched environmental conditions, but a wear-only group cannot also experience the specified corrosive environment without becoming a simultaneous wear-corrosion group. The noncorrosive wear-only environment is not defined.

The prediction requires total degradation to exceed the additive isolated losses while each component rate merely exceeds its corresponding baseline. The falsification rule instead appears to require mass loss, wear depth, and corrosion rate each to be compared with a sum of isolated degradations; wear depth and corrosion rate are not directly additive, and this is not the same criterion as the prediction.
